import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch. Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# Patch name -> branch name conversion.
is_patch = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_patch:
        # Patch ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

I published the lead's report as `202611/meeting_notes_event_refs/meeting_notes_event_refs.md` in the research repo, registered it as `research:202611/meeting_notes_event_refs/meeting_notes_event_refs.md` (`file:explicit:af58b39cf12d85fd1ebdee68`), and declared the commit. The host makes the commit after this turn ends.

**Source:** there was exactly one input that matched, `research:202611/meeting_notes_event_refs/meeting_notes_event_refs__final.md`. I read it with `sase artifact read`. I did not modify the lead's report, the drafts, or the diagram file.

**Layout:**
- The file opens with the title, then a research-query blockquote, then the infographic (`meeting_notes_event_refs_infographic.png`, which exists beside the report), then `## Bottom line` (the lead's Verdict).
- The sections that follow are: Explicit adjustments to the request → Facts every report converged on → The recommended design → First use case → Phasing → Risks worth keeping in view → Open questions for Bryan → Appendix: request and provenance.
- The design section holds the pipeline picture, the disagreements table, and subsections for command surface, library type, birth status, note body, AI and enrichment, producers, and event matching.
- No heading is numbered. Where a heading held a colon clause or code, I moved that text to a bold lead-in at the start of the section. The lead's byline and request restatement are now in the appendix.

**Checks against the lead's report:**
- Every non-heading line is still there word for word. The only exceptions are lines where I added a link or replaced a `§N` pointer.
- Every table cell is still there.
- The report now has 4 Mermaid diagrams: the lead's 1 plus 3 proposed ones.

**Diagrams:** the manifest's status was `ready` and its source matched the lead's label. All 3 diagrams are placed, each copied byte-for-byte inside its own anchored block and linked from exactly one reference sentence:
- `review-dependency` → `#figure-review-dependency` (after the birth-status paragraph)
- `recap-ownership` → `#figure-recap-ownership` (after the recap-ownership paragraph in the note-body section)
- `matching-fallback` → `#figure-matching-fallback` (after the event-matching paragraph)

None were left out. `pandoc` shows all three `figure-*` IDs.

**Links:**
- The lead's report has no external URLs or relative file links, so none needed checking or were dropped.
- Every `§N` pointer is now a link to the named section, because the PDF renumbers sections. Every internal link points to a heading or figure ID that `pandoc` confirms exists.
- **One correction:** the Bottom line's "(§7)" sits on the phrase "shipped today, by hand, before any code lands". Section 7 is the risks section, but the "today, by hand" path is in the lead's §5, so I treated it as a typo and linked it to `#first-use-case`. Change it back if you meant the risks section.

I didn't add the other registered images (`filing.png`, `where.png`, `prototype_pdf_page1.png`) because the lead's report doesn't use them.
